name: Weld-Drylands
geological_features: Welded tuff formations from ancient supervolcanic eruptions
Massive canyon systems cut through fused rock layers
Dust seas of powdered volcanic glass
specific_features: Pirate hideout in the canyon networks
description: Weld-Drylands is a desert world whose surface is dominated by welded tuff, the fused remnants of ancient supervolcanic eruptions that have solidified into a landscape of smooth, glass-like rock stretching to every horizon. Massive canyons have been carved through this fused layer by eons of thermal cycling and the abrasive action of dust-laden winds, creating a labyrinthine network of narrow defiles and broad valleys. The dust seas that fill the lowest basins are composed of pulverized volcanic glass, sharp enough to damage unprotected equipment.

The thin atmosphere offers little protection from the intense solar radiation, and the temperature differential between sun and shade is extreme enough that the welded tuff audibly cracks as the thermal boundary passes. The canyon walls display beautiful patterns where different eruption events created layers of different color and composition, geological strata readable like the pages of a violent history. At night, the volcanic glass dust catches starlight and the basins appear to glow faintly, a phenomenon that has misled more than one navigator into attempting a landing on what appeared to be illuminated terrain.

The canyon networks have attracted a pirate band that uses the narrow, confusing passages and the interference caused by the metallic rock to evade pursuit. Their base, deep in the most tortuous section of the canyon system, is virtually impossible to locate from orbit and difficult to approach from the ground. The welded tuff formations themselves are of geological interest, as the eruption events that created them were of a scale rarely seen in the catalogued systems.

The mineral resources of Weld-Drylands are modest but the welded tuff itself has applications as a construction material, being lightweight, strong, and readily cut into building blocks. The pirate presence makes commercial exploitation risky, and law enforcement operations in the canyons have consistently failed due to the terrain advantages the pirates enjoy. Recent seismic surveys suggest the volcanic activity that created the welded tuff is not entirely extinct, with a magma chamber detected at depth that could potentially power geothermal operations if safely accessed.
